messages.subject: Workshop on R
messages.body_plain:
Can we arrange any workshop on R?
Where experts working with R in different field can come and teach
something. It would enlarge the user base of R in India too.
messages.body_snippet:

messages.subject: RE: Workshop on R
messages.body_plain:
Hi,
That's a good idea Debasish. But since R being a very huge language, I would suggest that we should pick up a problem that industries are facing today and try solving and explaining through R.
Guys lets materialize this.
All the problems (hypothetical and practical) are welcome. We can discuss the problems and then we can have a workshop where we demonstrate out problems and solution.

Problems:
Q1 .Since R comes with a rich set of statistical functions and is very much suited for handling unstructured data, how can we leverage the power of R for solving big data problems?

Regards,
Som

messages.subject: RE: Workshop on R
messages.body_plain:
Vijay,

Could you be more specific about the type of examples you are trying to point?

 Well for the time series analysis what I can think as of now is that we can take a stock data problem to analyze the nature of a particular stock in specific period of time and predicting it? Of course this would be a somewhat difficult problem (atleast for me. I am not that much into Stocks and all), since you may be incorporating the BlackSchole or Monte Carlo simulation.

Well Guys on a serious note , whatever the problem statements we are proposing here and we wish to solve, we should also decide upon the  problem data set and YES if we can compare our R features with other languages that would be very great.  This could be taken as next step.

Some more problems:

Q5.  Demonstrating the Mandelbrot Set? This will expose the graphical capabilities of R.

Q6. Monte Carlo Simulation?

Regards,

Som

messages.subject: Re: Workshop on R
messages.body_plain:
Dear Friends,
In this regard, it would be better to start with basic stats and time series analysis. If we proceed gradually it may help us all. Even for me, I have been using some other tool for my analysis and now switching over to R, therefore, I need full understanding of some basic operations with R.

1.  Descriptive analysis.
2. Time series analysis (ARIMA, Volatility Modeling-ARCH, GARCH, EGARCH, M-GARCH etc.)

Problem data sets would any be regarding stocks, commodities etc. See, I think it is not the data set rather it is the procedure or understanding of R which is more important right at this stage.

Regards,
Debasish Maitra
Doctoral Participant
IRMA
Mob:09727885092
email...@irma.ac.in

messages.subject: Re: Workshop on R
messages.body_plain:
Dear Vijay,
what you are suggesting is absolutely right.
But do you know most of the problem arises when we don't start from basics. Even after this financial crisis, Alan Greenspan said that  basic correlation could not be modeled properly if so, then why the asset with negative correlation fell so sharply.

So, I feel if we spare sometimes (to brush through) on basic then graduate to the level of Time series analysis, it would bring in much more meaning.
Even we can prepare one concept note on this in MS-Word and send it to everybody then it would be easy for all of us to work on that concept note and come to a conclusion about what, where and how to proceed further??

What do you say...?

Regards,

Debasish Maitra
Doctoral Participant
IRMA
Mob:09727885092
email...@irma.ac.in

messages.body_plain:
Hi All,

I think the first meet of our workshop should not be dealt with very high level topics. We all are from various domains / back grounds so first of all we should know where we stand. And we all are facing similar kind of challenges with R in our own domains.

I seriously think we should not baffle the peoples on the very first meet.  We should make the people to appreciate the R first and then gradually we can expose much more complex problems in further meets. If people appreciate R and start using that  makes us win.

What do you say?

Regards,

Som

Regards

Vijay

Hi all,

I agree with the suggestions here that the first workshop should cover
the basics. By this I mean both in terms of basics of statistics, as
well as basics of R as a programming environment. In my experience, a
number of starting and beginner-intermediate users remain completely
unaware of a number of key concepts. If this is made clear in a
structured way, the user base will automatically increase.

Varun
